head: Swiss watches
were dying.
slides.sub: Then came a plastic watch with 51 parts.

image.label: A Swiss watchmaker’s bench at dusk, tools down
image.brief: 해 질 녘 스위스 시계 공방의 작업대. 공구가 내려져 있고 창밖은 눈 덮인 마을. 따뜻하지만 쓸쓸한 영화 같은 톤. 브랜드 로고 없음.

head: Then came
the quartz watch.
body: In the 1970s, cheap quartz watches from Japan and Hong Kong kept better time than Swiss mechanical ones, at a fraction of the price.
For generations, Switzerland had been the world’s watchmaker. Now it was losing the market fast.

image.label: Rows of cheap digital watches under shop lights
image.brief: 1970년대 상점 진열대에 가득한 값싼 디지털·쿼츠 시계들. 형광등 조명, 빨간 LED 숫자.

slides.label: of Swiss watch jobs disappeared between 1970 and the mid-1980s
body: Factories closed. The country’s two biggest watch groups were in such trouble that their banks brought in a consultant, Nicolas Hayek, to decide what could be saved.

image.label: An empty factory floor with covered machines
image.brief: 천으로 덮인 기계들이 늘어선 빈 시계 공장. 차가운 회색 빛.

head: Cheaper, more accurate rivals.
What do you do?
body: You run a struggling Swiss watch company. Your rivals sell better timekeeping for less.

options.text: Retreat to luxury mechanical watches, where margins are safe
options.feedback: Many Swiss makers did exactly this. It felt safe, but it handed the whole volume market to rivals. Keep swiping.

options.text: Build a cheap Swiss quartz watch to match their price
options.feedback: Close. Matching the price alone wasn’t enough, though. Keep swiping to see what else changed.

options.text: Make a cheap watch people buy as fashion, not as a clock
options.feedback: This is the path Swatch took. Keep swiping.

image.label: Two watches on a table: an old Swiss one and a cheap digital one
image.brief: 탁자 위 시계 두 개. 낡은 스위스 기계식 시계와 값싼 디지털 시계가 마주 보는 구도.

slides.label: parts in the first Swatch, far fewer than a typical watch
body: Engineers at ETA, a Swiss movement maker, rebuilt the watch from scratch. The movement went straight into a plastic case, robots could assemble it, and it couldn’t be opened or repaired. It didn’t need to be.

image.label: Exploded view of a simple plastic watch
image.brief: 단순한 플라스틱 시계의 분해도. 부품 수가 적다는 것이 한눈에 보이게. 실제 브랜드 디자인은 따라 하지 않음.

head: They didn’t sell a watch.
They sold a look.
body: Swatch launched in 1983 for under 50 Swiss francs, made in Switzerland. It came in bright colors, with new designs every season and editions made with artists.
People didn’t buy one. They bought several, to match outfits and moods.

image.label: A wrist stacked with colorful plastic watches
image.brief: 여러 개의 화려한 플라스틱 시계를 겹쳐 찬 손목. 1980년대 팝 컬러.

slides.label: Swatches sold by 1992, according to the company
body: The cheap end of the market, the part Swiss makers had given up on, became the base that paid for the comeback.

image.label: A wall of colorful watches in a 1990s store
image.brief: 1990년대 매장 벽면을 가득 채운 컬러풀한 시계 진열.

head: A cheap watch that
guarded the expensive ones.
body: Hayek argued that if the Swiss gave up the low end, rivals would use it as a step to climb higher. The group he led also owned luxury names like Omega.
Swatch held the bottom of the market, so no one could build from there.

image.label: A cheap watch and a luxury watch side by side
image.brief: 값싼 플라스틱 시계와 고급 시계가 나란히, 플라스틱 시계가 앞에서 막아서는 구도.

head: Don’t flee the low end.
Rebuild it.
body: Most leaders answer cheap rivals by moving upmarket, where margins feel safe. That retreat is how disruption usually wins.
Swatch went back to first principles: cut the watch to 51 parts, then turned a cheap product into one people bought for how it made them look.

image.label: Blueprint lines over a watch face
image.brief: 시계 문자판 위로 설계도 선이 겹쳐진 그래픽.

head: When cheap rivals come,
rethink the product.
body: Retreating upmarket feels safe, but it can hand rivals the next step.
**Try it today:** if you had to cut your product’s cost in half, what would you remove, and what could customers love instead?

image.label: A single bright watch on a dark background
image.brief: 어두운 배경 위 밝은 색 시계 하나.

factChecks.note: 스위스 시계 산업 일자리 감소 폭("약 3분의 2", 1970년~1980년대 중반)은 스위스시계산업연맹(FH) 통계로 확인하세요. 자료에 따라 1970년 약 9만 명에서 1980년대 중반 3만 명 안팎으로 나옵니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1970년 약 9만 명에서 1984~85년 3만~3만 3천 명으로 감소 확인(약 3분의 2).
은행이 Nicolas Hayek에게 ASUAG와 SSIH의 진단을 맡긴 시기와 두 회사 합병(1983)은 Swatch Group 공식 연혁으로 확인하세요.

부품 51개, ETA의 Elmar Mock·Jacques Müller 개발, 1983년 3월 취리히 출시는 Swatch 공식 자료 기준입니다. 출시 가격은 "50스위스프랑 미만"으로만 적었습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 부품 51개(당시 일반 무브먼트 약 91개), ETA의 Mock·Müller 개발, 1983년 3월 1일 취리히 출시 확인. 출시 가격은 미확인.
"1992년까지 1억 개 판매"는 회사 발표 수치입니다. 카드에도 "according to the company"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1992년 1억 번째 Swatch 확인.
저가 시장을 지켜야 고가 브랜드도 지킬 수 있다는 Hayek의 생각은 1993년 HBR 인터뷰 등에 나옵니다. 직접 인용 대신 풀어서 썼습니다.
